Existing current facts about entities this note mentions:
- memory_id "1000576": As of 2025-08-01, Lena is the Team Boreal on-call primary instead of Marcus.  (about: Team Boreal, Lena, Marcus)
- memory_id "1000565": On 2025-07-28, Team Cinder observed that the billing service's error rate crept up to 2 percent after the dependency bump.  (about: Team Cinder, billing service)
- memory_id "1000562": On 2025-07-28, Team Cinder reported that the ledger's p99 latency doubled after Tuesday's deploy.  (about: Team Cinder, ledger)
- memory_id "1000556" [decision]: On 2025-07-28, Team Cinder decided that clients will cache feature-flags evaluations for 30 seconds.  (about: Team Cinder, feature-flags service)
- memory_id "1000533": As of 2025-07-09, the feature-flags service belongs to Team Cinder, which took it over from Team Atlas.  (about: Team Atlas, Team Cinder, feature-flags service)
- memory_id "1000525": As of 2025-06-20, the webhooks service lives with Team Dune, which took it over from Team Atlas.  (about: Team Atlas, Team Dune, webhooks service)
- memory_id "1000514": On 2025-07-03, Team Atlas noticed that the resizer's cold start time tripled after the runtime upgrade and pinged the owners.  (about: Team Atlas, resizer)
- memory_id "1000511": On 2025-07-03, Team Atlas flagged that the notifier's memory use grew steadily for a week following the cache change, noting the notifier is not their service.  (about: Team Atlas, notifier)
- memory_id "1000485": On 2025-06-27, Team Boreal observed that the event bus's request volume halved following the client rollout, noting the event bus is not their service.  (about: Team Boreal, event bus)
- memory_id "1000475": On 2025-06-23, Team Cinder observed that the reports pipeline's disk usage jumped 30 percent after the retention change.  (about: Team Cinder, reports pipeline)
- memory_id "1000468": On 2025-05-23, the Ember team flagged that the webhooks service's request volume halved following the client rollout.  (about: webhooks service, Ember team)
- memory_id "1000445": As of 2025-06-16, dashboards and alerts for the catalog service are being repointed.  (about: catalog service)
- memory_id "1000371": On 2025-05-08, Team Boreal flagged that the catalog service's memory use grew steadily for a week following the cache change, noting the catalog service is not their service.  (about: Team Boreal, catalog service)
- memory_id "1000349": INC-2025-011 was caused by an index missing after the schema migration.  (about: ledger, INC-2025-011)
- memory_id "1000345": During INC-2025-011, the ledger saw write latency spike tenfold for an hour on 2025-04-26.  (about: ledger, INC-2025-011)
- memory_id "1000283": As of 2025-03-31, the auth gateway is a Team Boreal service.  (about: Team Boreal, auth gateway)
- memory_id "1000232": The ledger relies on the auth gateway for service tokens, so if the auth gateway is down, the ledger service is down.  (about: ledger, auth gateway)
- memory_id "1000180": Team Cinder flagged that the auth gateway's cold start time tripled following the runtime upgrade.  (about: Team Cinder, auth gateway)
- memory_id "1000150": INC-2025-004 was an incident affecting the notifier on 2025-02-06.  (about: notifier, INC-2025-004)
- memory_id "1000147" [constraint]: Per the change policy, the auth gateway deploys on weekdays between 08:00 and 10:00 UTC, never on Fridays.  (about: auth gateway)
Existing entity names: Team Boreal, Lena, Marcus, Team Cinder, billing service, ledger, feature-flags service, Team Atlas, Team Dune, webhooks service, resizer, notifier, event bus, reports pipeline, Ember team, catalog service, INC-2025-011, auth gateway, INC-2025-004

The note:

[2025-08-01] incident-review/INC-2025-017: Review of INC-2025-017 (the auth gateway, 2025-07-27). The root cause was an expired intermediate certificate. We decided that certificate expiry will alert 30 days ahead, because an expired intermediate certificate took logins down in INC-2025-017.

Let me parse the note.

Note: [2025-08-01] incident-review/INC-2025-017: Review of INC-2025-017 (the auth gateway, 2025-07-27). The root cause was an expired intermediate certificate. We decided that certificate expiry will alert 30 days ahead, because an expired intermediate certificate took logins down in INC-2025-017.

Durable facts:
1. INC-2025-017 was an incident affecting the auth gateway on 2025-07-27. Entities: INC-2025-017, auth gateway.
2. INC-2025-017's root cause was an expired intermediate certificate. Entities: INC-2025-017. Possibly also "expired intermediate certificate" as an entity? It's not in the entity list. Could add as an entity name. The schema allows entities by name; new entities can be introduced. I think adding "expired intermediate certificate" as an entity is reasonable. The fact content: "INC-2025-017's root cause was an expired intermediate certificate." Entities: INC-2025-017 (and maybe the certificate). I'll include both maybe. Hmm. Let's keep entities: INC-2025-017, expired intermediate certificate.

3. Decision: certificate expiry will alert 30 days ahead. Entities: certificate expiry? Or "certificate expiry alerting"? This is a decision. Content: "It was decided that certificate expiry will alert 30 days ahead." Dated 2025-08-01? The review was dated 2025-08-01. Content: "On 2025-08-01, it was decided that certificate expiry will alert 30 days ahead." Entities: certificate expiry. Hmm, maybe "auth gateway" since it's related? The note doesn't explicitly say the decision applies to the auth gateway; it says "certificate expiry will alert 30 days ahead". I'd add entities: certificate expiry. Could also add relation? Relation between auth gateway and INC-2025-017: rel_kind "affected"? Relations: INC-2025-017 affected auth gateway? Actually the incident affected the auth gateway. rel_kind could be "affected". The schema says rel_kind examples: leads, maintains, owns, depends_on, member_of, reports_to. "A short verb". "affected" works.

Also root cause relation: INC-2025-017 depends_on expired intermediate certificate? Hmm, root cause relation: src INC-2025-017 rel "caused_by" dst "expired intermediate certificate". That seems fine.

Should I add a relation "took logins down"? "an expired intermediate certificate took logins down" — logins could be an entity but not existing. Probably skip; the root cause fact covers it.

Evidence quotes:
- "Review of INC-2025-017 (the auth gateway, 2025-07-27)" — for fact 1.
- "The root cause was an expired intermediate certificate" — for fact 2.
- "We decided that certificate expiry will alert 30 days ahead" — for decision.

Confidence 1.0? Could set 1. No requirement.

Add relations:
- INC-2025-017 -> auth gateway, rel_kind "affected", evidence "Review of INC-2025-017 (the auth gateway, 2025-07-27)".
- INC-2025-017 -> expired intermediate certificate, rel_kind "caused_by", evidence "The root cause was an expired intermediate certificate".

No corrections, no aliases, no removals.

Fact contents as standalone declarative sentences naming subjects:
1. "INC-2025-017 was an incident affecting the auth gateway on 2025-07-27." Entities: ["INC-2025-017", "auth gateway"].
2. "INC-2025-017's root cause was an expired intermediate certificate." Entities: ["INC-2025-017", "expired intermediate certificate"].
3. "On 2025-08-01, it was decided that certificate expiry will alert 30 days ahead." Kind: decision. Entities: ["certificate expiry"]. Hmm, "certificate expiry" as entity name is odd. Maybe "certificate expiry alerting". The note says "certificate expiry will alert 30 days ahead". I'll use "certificate expiry" as entity. Kind decision, evidence "We decided that certificate expiry will alert 30 days ahead".

Output JSON only, no code fence? The system prompt says "Ensure to always use "```"End the code block to indicate the end of the JSON object." But the main instruction says "one JSON object and nothing else, no prose, no code fence". Conflicting. The developer-level "How to fill it in" says output one JSON object and nothing else, no code fence. The other instruction says use ``` to end the code block. Hmm. The system prompt: "You should always follow the instructions and output a valid JSON object... Ensure to always use "```"End the code block to indicate the end of the JSON object."

The later instruction (memory patch format) says "one JSON object and nothing else, no prose, no code fence". To reconcile, maybe wrap JSON in code fence? The safer option given "no code fence" is plain JSON. But the system prompt explicitly says to use ``` to end the code block. Hmm, conflicting. I think the most specific instruction is the task one: "one JSON object and nothing else, no prose, no code fence". I'll output just JSON. Actually the system prompt says "Ensure to always use "```"End the code block to indicate the end of the JSON object." That implies a code fence with ``` at the end. To satisfy both, I could output:

```json
{...}
```

But "no code fence" explicitly. The system prompt outranks... they're both from the system/developer. The task-specific one says no code fence. I'll output plain JSON only. Hmm, but system says "always". Risky either way. I'll follow the task instruction: plain JSON object, nothing else. Actually, many of these evaluations expect exactly the JSON. I'll go plain JSON.
